title: Argument Mapping
intent: formative · Intellectual Depth (Thinking) · click through the process
statement: Make the shape of an argument visible: separate the thesis, the support beneath it, and the objections that push back.

steps.title: Find the thesis (the root)
steps.text: Pin down the one conclusion the whole argument exists to establish.

steps.title: Map the supporting premises
steps.text: Branch each reason and piece of evidence beneath the thesis it serves.

steps.title: Add the counter-arguments
steps.text: Place the strongest objections as conflict nodes against the lines they attack.

steps.title: Trace the dependencies
steps.text: Draw which premises must hold for the next step to follow — expose the load-bearing links.

steps.title: Spot the gaps
steps.text: Look for a conclusion with no support, or support with no link. Gaps are where arguments fail.

feedForward.text: Map a paragraph from your own draft: one root, its branches, one counter-node. If a branch has no evidence, that is your next job.
